Instrument (EN): Kessler-6 Psychological Distress Scale — Swedish population revalidation (existing official translation)
Scales / measured domains (EN): One supported general non-specific psychological distress scale (30-day recall). Exploratory split into anxiety 2 / depression 4 NOT empirically separable here (factor correlation .99); failed bifactor estimation.
Research provenance: Ehnsiö K, Tiikkaja S, Pellas J. BMC Psychology 2026-10-23 DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05857-9; 2022 Life and Health Mid-Sweden survey N31759 adults aged 18–102. One-factor omega .883-.899, CFI .996, RMSEA .069; configural/metric invariance gender and age supported but not scalar; no Swedish clinical cutoffs validated. Used pre-existing official Swedish translation; earlier Swedish evaluation in 2024, not a newly created 2026 translation.
DB locales: Published LIVE DB already has parent k6 key EN; THIS exact SV-SE edition/study key absent, no new website locale.
EN form: EN global source scale is NOT a new English adaptation; existing LIVE K6 EN.
RU form: No new RU validation in this Swedish cohort.
ES form: No new ES validation in this Swedish cohort.
Other translations: SV-SE: existing Swedish respondent translation by Stockholm Centre for Epidemiology and Community Medicine, independently re-examined in N31759. Official Kessler site lists Swedish version, plus various other translations for unrestricted use; listed files alone do NOT prove locale-specific psychometric validity.
Target population: 31,759 population-survey adults in five Mid-Sweden regions (18–102); cross-sectional population not a diagnostically adjudicated clinical sample.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: OFFICIAL RIGHTS EVIDENCE: Kessler's Harvard-hosted copyright owner's page explicitly states K6/K10 use free with no formal permission, translations posted for unrestricted use, requires copyright acknowledgment and 2003 citation. This is stronger than paper CC; before commercial clinical deployment still verify EXACT Swedish form/scoring version, legal attribution and safety, calibrated cutoffs, sensitive mental-health data safeguards.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / RIGHTS_REVIEW, despite source instrument unrestricted use. Re-validation of existing Swedish edition, NOT new translation; general distress 1 factor ONLY, no separate diagnosis/cutoffs, Swedish thresholds require clinical ROC research; do not deploy or alter existing EN k6.

Instrument (EN): Adaptive Cognition and Behaviors about Sleep-6 — original scale and independent insomnia-symptom sample psychometric study
Scales / measured domains (EN): Adaptive sleep-related cognition (4 items) and adaptive sleep-related behavior (2 items); not interchangeable with DBAS-6 maladaptive belief items.
Research provenance: Original Chung S et al., Sleep Medicine 2025 DOI 10.1016/j.sleep.2025.106703 developed ACBS-6 in Korean general population. Lee J et al. BMC Psychology 2026-10-23 DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05683-z online sample of N600 participants REPORTING insomnia symptoms; CFA two-factor/IRT Rasch+GRM; items 3 and 4 limited information, ISI correlation -.13. Original development and 2026 N600 study distinct; cross-section does NOT establish treatment responsiveness or clinically calibrated cutoffs.
DB locales: No ACBS-6 source/edition key in Master3893, 11 registered, PR495 386-key source or LIVE Supabase published definitions.
EN form: English-language paper does NOT prove validated EN respondent questionnaire.
Other translations: Original instrument developed in Korean general-population setting, revalidated in Korean clinical recruitment setting, BUT actual administered language/cross-cultural equivalence not independently documented in accessible abstracts; KO-KR respondent form NOT marked validated translation and no EN/RU/ES version claimed.
Target population: Original Korean adults; re-validation: 600 online respondents reporting insomnia symptoms; not diagnosis-confirmed insomnia cohort.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: 2026 validation article CC BY 4.0 is NOT confirmation of commercial rights for original 2025 Elsevier source scale (copyright reserved). Obtain owners' authorization for commercial hosted form, exact item wording, 4+2 scoring, translations and use of item 3/4 before activation.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. No version-specific commercial digital licence, original participant language not certified. Modest criterion correlation, no clinical thresholds; not diagnosis, no automatic live test.

Instrument (EN): Psychosocial Adaptation Scale for Stroke — 31-item five-factor China development (PASS)
Scales / measured domains (EN): Five factors extracted and CFA-supported; names, item allocations and authorized scoring map NOT specified in publicly accessible early online abstract and require exact supplementary/full-form review.
Research provenance: Zhang Q, Li X, Yue M et al., BMC Psychology 2026-10-23 DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05768-9. China stroke survivor sample N441; Delphi, cognitive interviews, EFA/CFA, 31 retained items and five factors; Cronbach alpha .874-.961, retest .783-.953; PAIS-SR r .642 and SSQOL r -.534. Early citable article, full factor labels/scoring need further verification.
DB locales: Not the unrelated PASS-18 procrastination scale already in research registry; no PASS-stroke source/edition key in Master3893, registered snapshot or PR495.
EN form: No EN clinical respondent edition evidenced from article in English.
Other translations: Original studied population China. Available abstract does not state actual administered questionnaire language; do not label ZH-CN adaptation or independently validated Chinese translation without respondent evidence.
Target population: 441 people with stroke in China; specialized rehabilitation context; cannot extend norms to non-stroke/general-wellbeing populations.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Article rights CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial/no derivatives) and separate instrument wording/rights unconfirmed. Explicit authorization for paid digital clinical hosting and derivatives, full questions/item-factor scoring, therapist oversight and stroke-related consent/privacy required.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY, distinct from PASS procrastination. Factor names not proven; do NOT invent named scales/cutoffs, deploy, or claim Chinese translation due study country.

Instrument (EN): Patient Health Questionnaire-4 — contextual two-factor validation in returned Cambodian migrant workers
Scales / measured domains (EN): Depression/PHQ-2 (2 items); Anxiety/GAD-2 (2 items); optional overall distress, TWO correlated factors supported in this context.
Research provenance: Chien S, Liu K-L, Khov H, Chan C-C. Discover Psychology 2026-10-23 DOI 10.1007/s44202-026-00945-8. N392 returnee migrant workers in four Cambodia provinces recruited October 2022; Cronbach alpha .78, two-factor CFA CFI .99 TLI .98 RMSEA .035 SRMR .016, latent factor r .79. Cross-sectional occupational exposure associations; no new language-specific cutoffs or independent longitudinal diagnostic calibration.
DB locales: Parent phq-4 is LIVE EN in DB and research Master; THIS Cambodian-study contextual evidence is new distinct study/edition key, not a new 4-question test family or deployed locale.
EN form: Existing PHQ-4 EN form is not newly validated by this context-specific Cambodian sample.
Other translations: Cambodia study does NOT explicitly identify Khmer-language administered form, forward/back translation or Khmer scoring; DO NOT claim KH-KH/KM-KH validated adaptation from country alone.
Target population: 392 adult returned Cambodian migrant workers in four high-migration provinces; 52% male and mean age 34.7; no Cambodian population or clinical norms established.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: 2026 paper CC BY covers article but not automatically every PHQ-4 author/version permission. Verify exact respondent language, attribution, rights for specific hosted form, clinical safety, appropriate country-specific cutoffs and lawful protected health-data flow; existing EN published PHQ-4 unchanged.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY, contextual validation of existing PHQ-4, NOT new Khmer test or language. Distinct key DOI/context, no site or live DB modifications.
